slides.heading: Merge Overlapping Intervals
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Merge Overlapping Intervals, a medium arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Merge all overlapping [start, end] intervals; result sorted by start.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Merge all overlapping start, end intervals; result sorted by start.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: After sorting by start, overlapping intervals are adjacent, so one pass can merge them.
slides.narration: After sorting by start, overlapping intervals are adjacent, so one pass can merge them.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: repeatedly merge any overlapping pair → O(n²) or worse
Optimal: sort by start, single sweep → O(n log n)
After sorting, only the last merged interval can overlap
slides.narration: Repeatedly scanning for any overlapping pair is at least quadratic. Once intervals are sorted by start, an interval can only overlap the most recent merged one, so a single sweep finishes the job after an n log n sort.

slides.heading: Approach
slides.narration: Step by step. First, sort by start. Second, keep the current merged interval. Third, extend its end on overlap. Fourth, otherwise start a new one.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: [1,2] no overlap → start new interval
slides.narration: Interval 1 to 2: it starts after the last merged interval ends, so it begins a new one.

slides.narration: Interval 3 to 5: it starts after the last merged interval ends, so it begins a new one.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: [4,7] overlaps → extend to [3, 7]
slides.narration: Interval 4 to 7: it starts before the last merged interval ends, so we extend that interval's end to 7.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: [6,8] overlaps → extend to [3, 8]
slides.narration: Interval 6 to 8: it starts before the last merged interval ends, so we extend that interval's end to 8.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: [9,10] no overlap → start new interval
slides.narration: Interval 9 to 10: it starts after the last merged interval ends, so it begins a new one.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We clone and sort by start. For each interval, if the last merged interval's end reaches its start, we extend that end to the max; otherwise we append a copy.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n log n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Fully contained intervals: take max of ends
slides.narration: Touching endpoints count as overlapping, which is why we compare with greater-or-equal. A contained interval is handled by taking the max of the ends.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: insert a new interval into a sorted list
slides.narration: Follow-ups include inserting one interval into an already merged list, or counting overlapping meetings.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: After sorting by start, overlapping intervals are adjacent, so one pass can merge them.
slides.narration: To recap Merge Overlapping Intervals: After sorting by start, overlapping intervals are adjacent, so one pass can merge them. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
